$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository, a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json
through the ts-bridge port, trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. Precedent for
a per-repo port: kubelab, hive, web and ts-bridge each carry their own copy; the SSOT of the
SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all -- `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`, exit 1 (measured 2026-09-06). Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND
when the question cannot be computed, so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear
one. But a check that reports the same thing every time it runs stops being read.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over every non-Dependabot
pull request (#1..#62), reading `issues/<n>/comments` for what CodeRabbit actually posts:
## Walkthrough              -> #36 #39 #56          (a review ran; this is the attesting marker)
## Review limit reached     -> #37 #38 #40 #57      (also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai')
## Review skipped           -> #61 #62              (path filters: only site/package-lock.json changed)
(no CodeRabbit output)      -> #1..#18              (CodeRabbit was not installed yet)
(no CodeRabbit output)      -> every Dependabot PR  (excluded by the app's configuration)
So of the nine PRs CodeRabbit could have reviewed, three were reviewed, four were declined on
quota and two were skipped. The limit and skipped headings sit inside a `> ` blockquote in the
comment body, so they match by substring, never by line start.
'No actionable comments were generated in the recent review' (the dotfiles clean-run marker)
does appear here, on #36 and #39, but only alongside `## Walkthrough` on the same comment, so
it adds no PR that the walkthrough marker does not already attest. It is left out rather than
carried as a second marker that would look measured and assert nothing extra.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool,
which scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change, and in this repo the decline is the majority case: of the nine PRs it could have reviewed (#36..#62, non-Dependabot), four drew 'Review limit reached' and two 'Review skipped'. A decline that REFUSED would make the gate red more often than green and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here: suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here (kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot], dotfiles 172). It has NEVER been observed in yt-metrics-cli, because the workflow landed in the same change as this file and NAN_API_KEY is not set in this repository yet: until the owner runs `dotf secrets sync ci --repo mlorentedev/yt-metrics-cli` and a PR-Agent run goes green, this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #57, #40, #16, #13 and #9: exactly these three paths every time (release-type python bumps the version in pyproject.toml, which is why this signature has one file more than the ts-bridge one; #7 predates the manifest and touched CHANGELOG.md alone). Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch: release-please runs under a human PAT here (RELEASE_TOKEN, author mlorentedev), so an author rule would not fire, and a branch rule would let any branch named to match walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
